body:
## Goal
Establish the single persistent on-disk store, its schema, an idempotent migration runner, and the npm script surface every other unit plugs into.

## Spec
This unit is the sole owner of the schema; the API, worker, and admin CLI depend on it and never define schema changes themselves.

Store: a single on-disk SQLite database file (e.g. Node's built-in node:sqlite) at a path configurable by env with a repo-local default — never an in-memory store, so all data survives a process restart. No external web framework or ORM.

Schema (owned only here): users (id, unique username, password hash column, an `active` flag defaulting to active); projects (id, name, owner_id -> users, created_at); tasks (id, title, project_id -> projects, done flag defaulting to false, created_at); export_jobs (id, project_id, status, a column to hold the produced report, created_at); plus whatever bookkeeping table the migration runner needs to record applied migrations, and a token/session persistence table if bearer tokens are stored server-side (the API unit decides token mechanism, but any persisted token state lives in this schema). Passwords are stored only as a hash — the plaintext password is never persisted (security invariant; the hashing itself is implemented by the API unit).

Migration runner: applies pending migrations in order, records which have been applied, and is safe to run repeatedly — a second run when already current applies nothing and still exits 0. Expose a programmatic entry (e.g. an exported migrate()) so the API server can apply pending migrations on boot without shelling out.

package.json gains "migrate", "start", and "admin" scripts. "migrate" runs this runner; "start" and "admin" point at entrypoints the later units create (src/index.js and the admin CLI) — scaffolding all three scripts here keeps package.json out of the other units' change sets so they can be delivered in parallel.

## Changes
- `src/store/db.js` — creates
- `src/store/schema.js` — creates
- `src/store/migrate.js` — creates
- `package.json` — refactors-existing
- `test/store.migrate.test.js` — creates

## Acceptance
- [ ] AC-1: On a fresh checkout `npm run migrate` exits 0 and creates the on-disk store file at the configured (default) path
- [ ] AC-2: Re-running is a no-op when current: a second `npm run migrate` exits 0 and applies no further migrations
- [ ] AC-3: The store is on-disk, not in-memory: after the migrate process exits, a store file still exists on disk at the store path (data survives a restart)
- [ ] AC-4: package.json defines "migrate", "start", and "admin" scripts
- [ ] AC-5: The schema defines users (with an `active` flag defaulting to active), projects, tasks, and export_jobs, and users store only a password hash — no plaintext-password column exists
- [ ] AC-6: A programmatic migration entry point is exported so the API server can apply pending migrations on boot: `node --test test/store.migrate.test.js` exercises it and exits 0

## Verify
- node --test test/store.migrate.test.js (unit)
- npm run migrate (validate)
- npm run typecheck (validate)

## Non-Goals
- HTTP endpoints, the worker loop, or the admin CLI behavior (their own units)
- Password hashing implementation (the API unit owns it; this unit only reserves the hash column)
